story.title: What to decide
story.lede: One unplanned decision to check, one coverage gap to keep visible.

items.text: To answer a Qodo finding, the agent changed the shared perf comparison tool, which the plan kept out of scope. A comparison whose base predates this PR now gives no metric rows and asks a person. Decide whether that is the right trade.
Qodo's review of the final merge commit reports status completed but review_complete=false, so zero open findings is not a complete review.

story.title: One CSV row per published day
story.lede: The headless performance recorder writes a row for every published day, not one per batch, and still exits 6 when a day is missing.

paragraphs.label: Today
paragraphs.text: The recorder takes one snapshot per batch of committed days. When the host delivers two days together, one of them never gets a row, so a quick performance run sometimes exports 49 of 50 rows and the whole comparison fails with exit 6.

paragraphs.label: Why
paragraphs.text: Issue 82: one lost row made a performance comparison of another PR fail even though the simulation results matched. The ticket asks for exactly one row per measured day and says exit 6 must still fire when rows really are missing.

paragraphs.label: What
paragraphs.text: Each published day record becomes its own row with its own day, generation and commit time. Export waits for the final measured day. The row check accepts the CSV only when it holds exactly the expected days in order.

paragraphs.label: How
paragraphs.text: The recorder subscribes to the host's ordered day records instead of the per-batch tick. The headless runner's row check reads the committed-day column and requires first_day, first_day+1, ... with no gaps.

contributions.adds: Per-day capture in the recorder, a date-order row check in the headless runner, and tests for batched, late and missing days.

story.title: From a published day to the exit code
story.lede: A day record travels from the host to the recorder, into the CSV, and back through the row check.

story.title: Ticket acceptance criteria
story.lede: Two of three criteria are shown by evidence in the PR; the third is a scope rule.

items.why: Box unchecked in the PR body. The agent report says all 128 default checks reported PASS but the wrapper's aggregate exit was unavailable. The focused recorder test passes locally (93 checks, 0 failures).

story.title: Refuse comparisons across the recorder change?
story.lede: The recorder now times days from worker commit stamps, not the main-thread clock. Qodo flagged that a base-before/head-after comparison would report a throughput change that comes only from the new method. The agent made the comparison tool refuse such pairs.
story.ask: Accept that any comparison spanning PR 85 returns needs_human with no metric rows, or ask for a different handling (for example re-measuring the base with the new recorder)?
options: Accept: no numbers is better than numbers that mean different things
Ask the owner how perf PRs branched before PR 85 should be judged

hrhgit/Project.Keynes#85.summary: Fixes issue 82: the headless performance recorder writes one row per published day and the runner rejects a CSV with a short count or a gap in the dates. After Qodo's first review, the agent also changed the shared comparison tool tools/perf/perf_change_check.py so that runs recorded with different recorder methods are never compared metric by metric. This review follows that decision. The docs, perf_recorder_graph.gd and the other runner changes were not read in depth; their lines stay outside the layers.
hrhgit/Project.Keynes#85.risk: Low for game behavior (test and tooling code only; native_changed=false). The consequence is for the factory's perf merge gate: a perf PR whose merge base predates PR 85 gets needs_human instead of a metric comparison, and archived method-2 records are no longer reused.

layers.title: Recorder method in the comparison tool
layers.summary: The decision under review: METHOD_VERSION 3, a recorder_method per run, and assess() refusing to compare different methods.

decisions.text: The perf comparison refuses to compare runs recorded with different recorder methods: needs_human, no metric rows
decisions.plan: The plan names only headless_perf_record.gd, perf_recorder.gd and perf_recorder_test.gd, says 'The benchmark requires numeric tick_idx, speed_multiplier, and t_sus_ms on every row', and step 4 says 'Verify the diff contains only recorder and test files.'
decisions.why: Commit 2ba168376 ('address Qodo findings ...5844bc28...') answers Qodo's Medium finding 'Headline throughput changes meaning across this commit': throughput now comes from worker produced_at_us stamps instead of the main-thread clock, and archived records were keyed only by METHOD_VERSION = 2, so a base-before/head-after compare would report a change caused by the method. The agent bumped METHOD_VERSION to 3, made the runner print recorder_method, labels old scripts unversioned:<script hash>, and has assess() return needs_human when the two sides differ. It also makes t_sus_ms empty in the daily CSV (Qodo finding 2c087197: a fake zero).
decisions.notice: A comparison whose base predates PR 85 still checks the daily result hashes but gives no metric rows and exits 2 (needs_human); the factory's merge gate stops on needs_human.

decisions.text: Exit 6 fires on a short count or on any gap or reordering in the committed-day column
decisions.plan: Issue 82, item 2: 'Do not relax the check: exit 6 must still fire when rows really are missing.'
decisions.why: The agent's own plan (PR body, step 3) chose to 'Check the exact date sequence and retain exit 6 for a genuinely short CSV.' No further rationale is recorded. Reviewer's reading: the recorder skips a day it never receives, so a count-only check could pass a CSV whose count matches while a day is missing; checking the dates closes that hole.
decisions.notice: Context only in this review: a run that loses a day fails with 'CSV days must be ordered from N through M'.

quality.summary: tools/perf unit tests pass at the merge commit (75 tests, OK). test_refuses_throughput_comparison_between_different_recorder_methods asserts needs_human, no rows and the 'incompatible recorder methods' reason. A real compare of base c81ebf871 against merge 62ba798d6 is the behavior check.

tests.why: Lines 571-585 build a base with unversioned:foreground and a head with day_records_worker_v1, double the head throughput, and assert needs_human with no rows, so a method change cannot pass as a speedup.
Context: the missing-day test that guards the exit 6 decision.

files.headline: Rows come from day records, not from batch ticks.

lines.text: Each published day record within the measurement window appends one row with its own day, generation and commit time.
A replayed day (day <= last published) is skipped, so a duplicate batch adds no row.

files.headline: The row check reads the dates.

lines.text: Exit 6 now requires the committed-day column to read first_day, first_day+1, ... in order, in addition to the expected row count.
When the count matches but the dates do not, the error says the days must be ordered from first through last.

files.headline: Tests cover batched, late and missing days.

lines.text: Days 6 and 8 delivered without 7: exit 6 with the expected count 3, and still exit 6 when the expected count is 2.

files.headline: The comparison tool knows which recorder produced a run.

lines.text: Different recorder methods on base and head: status needs_human, rows empty, reason 'incompatible recorder methods'. Daily result hashes are still compared.
METHOD_VERSION goes from 2 to 3, so archived records made with method 2 are not reused.
Scripts without a recorder_method marker are labelled unversioned:<sha256 of the runner script>.
